summary: The health-tech sector is grappling with fundamental challenges across AI implementation, economic incentives, and infrastructure resilience. In AI development, pharmaceutical companies are discovering that computational power and data volume are not the limiting factors—rather, the lack of standardized clinical terminology and semantic frameworks is preventing AI systems from reasoning meaningfully over real-world data. On the payor side, there's growing recognition that focusing narrowly on medication costs while ignoring broader cost-effectiveness metrics and downstream system risks ultimately harms both patients and overall healthcare spending. In infrastructure news, Louisiana received new federal funding to support rural health innovation, while a major cybersecurity exercise called Operation Vital Signs tested the health sector's ability to respond to coordinated cyber attacks. Leadership shifts are also underway, with digital health company Omada Health appointing a new CEO as part of broader personnel changes in the sector.
